glossary.entries.arms.body.0: Longarm has a telescopic arm: how far it reaches depends on the cell’s own data, such as reaching left by as many cells as “this item’s weight”, so it can read cells outside its view.
glossary.entries.arms.body.1: Under the view is the arm’s own row, showing the cells it can reach; click one, and the “View” part gains an output that reads it.
glossary.entries.arms.title: Telescopic arm
glossary.entries.sweep.body.0: Broom has a sweep arm: it sweeps a whole run of cells in one go and feeds every number in the run into the circuit board, however many cells the run has.
glossary.entries.sweep.body.1: A wire carrying a whole segment is drawn thicker. Mergers, Adders and Multipliers take a whole segment directly, and every number in it takes part; gates do not take segments.
glossary.entries.sweep.title: Sweep Arm
